title: COUNT vs COUNTA: numbers only, or everything?
meta_desc: COUNT vs COUNTA: what each one actually counts (numbers vs any non-empty cell), the blank-vs-empty-string trap, and verified behavior across Excel, Google Sheets, and LibreOffice.
intro: They look like twins but count different things: COUNT tallies only numbers, while COUNTA tallies every cell that isn't empty — text, dates, errors, TRUE/FALSE and all. Picking the wrong one is the classic reason a 'how many rows' total comes out too low or too high.

cols: Numbers only (incl. dates & times, which are numbers)
Any non-empty cell — text, numbers, errors, logicals
COUNTED — the cell isn't truly empty (the classic trap)
Universal — identical in every Excel, Sheets & LibreOffice version we test

when.use_when: You want 'how many numeric entries' — amounts filled in, measurements taken, scores recorded. Text labels and blanks are correctly skipped.
You want 'how many rows have anything' — names entered, tickets logged, any non-empty response. Watch out for cells holding a formula's "" result, which COUNTA still counts.

compat_note: Both execute identically across every version of all three apps we test. The one behavior that surprises people isn't a compat difference — it's that a cell containing =IF(...,"") is NOT empty, so COUNTA includes it and COUNTBLANK excludes it. To count only visually-blank cells, use COUNTBLANK; to count numbers, COUNT; to count real entries including text, COUNTA.
